title: Senefelder develops printing from stone
summary: Alois Senefelder experimented with printing from stone and developed the chemical principle used in lithography, seeking an inexpensive way to reproduce texts and music.

claims.text: Alois Senefelder experimented with printing from stone and developed the chemical principle used in lithography, seeking an inexpensive way to reproduce texts and music.
The Met catalogue distinguishes 1796 relief-printing experiments from the 1798 chemical discovery; its overview compresses the invention to “around 1796.”
Greasy marks accept oily ink while a damp treated surface resists it. The method opened new possibilities for reproducing drawings.

review.corroboration: Two Met accounts were compared. Their dates describe different stages; the record uses a development interval. National Galleries of Scotland retrieval failed and is not cited.
